comparison: Perfect agreement on high-throughput screening methodology (C36-C41). Both evaluations found the assay design, quality controls (Z'-factor), pilot validation, and hit identification process to be well-supported. Peer reviewers described the assay as 'clever' and OpenEval noted 'excellent assay quality.'

Perfect agreement on negative results from initial inhibitor testing (C34-C35). Both evaluations accepted these findings as valid justification for the high-throughput screening approach. OpenEval explicitly noted the negative results were 'clearly documented' and peer reviewers implicitly accepted this as part of the logical experimental progression.

Perfect agreement on structure-activity relationship findings (C50-C52). Both evaluations supported the SAR campaign identifying key functional groups. OpenEval noted the limited sample size (4 analogs) but found conclusions reasonable, while peer reviewers accepted the findings without critique.

Perfect agreement on crystallographic validation (C67). Both evaluations accepted the structural evidence that the valine mutation creates additional space without major perturbations. OpenEval noted the limitation to static crystal structure, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted this as part of well-controlled experimental design.

Strong agreement on allosteric mechanism (C53-C56). Both evaluations found the Lineweaver-Burk plot data and mechanistic characterization well-supported. Peer reviewers described experiments as 'well-controlled' and explicitly stated the allosteric mechanism was demonstrated, matching OpenEval's assessment.

Strong agreement on HDX-MS mechanistic insights (C57-C60). Both evaluations accepted the differential deuterium exchange patterns and mechanistic interpretation. Peer reviewers specifically highlighted 'compelling evidence' for how gatekeeper changes sensitize to allosteric inhibitors, while OpenEval noted the putative nature without high-resolution structural data.

Substantial agreement on gatekeeper mutation preserving activity (C27-C30). OpenEval found claims well-supported by sequence alignment and kinetic data. Peer reviewers praised the finding as 'serendipitous' and 'interesting,' though peer R1 also includes kinetic parameters (C31-C33) and cellular activity (C61) not in OpenEval R1.

Agreement on Michaelis-Menten kinetics (C31-C33). OpenEval found the kinetic measurements well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the overall validation that the valine mutation 'didn't affect enzymatic activity,' grouping these claims with gatekeeper mutation data.

Agreement on FMP-201300 selectivity (C47-C49). OpenEval found NMR assay data well-supported with appropriate replicates. Peer reviewers explicitly confirmed the ~10-fold selectivity for L210V over WT and noted this selectivity was maintained for IP6K2. Peer R3 also includes C3 and C44 not in OpenEval R7.

Agreement on flavonoid dismissal (C42-C43). OpenEval found the dismissal justified by citations documenting promiscuous activity. Peer reviewers did not challenge this decision and implicitly accepted the focus on FMP-201300 as the appropriate non-polyphenolic hit.

Both address FMP-201300 selectivity. OpenEval R5 covers screening data and selectivity demonstration (C42-C44), while peer R3 emphasizes the ~10-fold selectivity finding (C44) along with NMR validation (C47-C49). Both evaluations support the selectivity claims.

Agreement on compound characterization (C45-C46, C62). OpenEval found literature searches, structural analysis, and toxicity testing well-supported. Peer reviewers accepted these characterization data without question as part of 'well-controlled' experiments, with peer R7 grouping C62 with C45-C46.

Both address cellular activity validation. OpenEval R11 covers kinetic data, toxicity, and cellular assays (C61-C63), while peer R1 includes C61 as part of the overall validation that the mutation approach works. Both evaluations support these claims.

Overlap on cellular validation (C63-C64). OpenEval R11 addresses cellular activity and medicinal chemistry context, while peer R9 focuses on cellular validation data. Both evaluations accepted the cellular evidence without challenge.

Overlap on toxicity data (C62). OpenEval R11 includes toxicity testing as part of compound validation, while peer R7 groups toxicity with other characterization data (C45-C46). Both evaluations support these findings.

Agreement on biological context and motivation (C1-C2, C6-C9). OpenEval found these claims well-supported by literature citations. Peer reviewers did not challenge the background, implicitly accepting the established context. Peer R12 covers broader introduction claims (C1-C17) than OpenEval R13.

Agreement on limitations of genetic methods (C10-C14). OpenEval found these claims supported by citations to previous studies. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this rationale as part of the introduction without challenge, grouping with other background claims.

Agreement on current state of IP6K inhibitors (C15-C17). OpenEval found these claims supported by recent literature. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this context as part of the comprehensive introduction without critique.

Agreement on analog-sensitive approach background (C18-C22). OpenEval found the description of established methodology well-supported by foundational citations. Peer reviewers accepted this methodological framework, describing the overall approach as 'elegant.' Peer R13 also includes gatekeeper identification (C23-C27).

Agreement on challenges with non-protein kinases (C23-C26). OpenEval found these claims supported by previous studies. Peer reviewers accepted this rationale without critique as part of the methodological background, grouping with analog-sensitive approach claims.

Agreement on discussion context (C68-C70). OpenEval found these claims supported by citations. Peer reviewers accepted the discussion without challenge and explicitly stated the work 'will undoubtedly inspire other analog-sensitive inhibitor studies.' Peer R14 covers broader discussion claims (C68-C77).

Key difference in evaluation certainty. OpenEval rated mechanistic speculation about binding mode (C71-C75) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct structural evidence, noting claims are 'largely speculative' despite plausible analogies to EGFR inhibitors. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the discussion and broader implications without challenging the speculative nature.

Agreement on medicinal chemistry considerations (C64-C65). OpenEval found these claims supported by established knowledge. Peer reviewers accepted this as reasonable future direction without challenge.

Overlap on carboxylic acid groups (C64). OpenEval R20 addresses medicinal chemistry context for these groups, while peer R9 implicitly accepts cellular validation despite the presence of carboxylic acids. Both evaluations support the claims.

Agreement on conclusions and future utility (C76-C77). OpenEval found conclusions reasonable based on experimental findings, noting C77 is appropriately framed as potential rather than demonstrated. Peer reviewers accepted the broader implications and explicitly endorsed the work's value for inspiring future studies.
